mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate decreases and unemployment rate increases, it signals economic stress, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as investors seek safer assets.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by 0.25% and UNRATE increases by 0.2pp
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market weakness
failure_condition: If the specified trigger occurs but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production suggests strong economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If payroll employment increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 45% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates reduced demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts decline but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales increase and interest rates decrease, consumer spending boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.

regime_hint: low interest rate environment with consumer spending growth
failure_condition: If the specified trigger occurs but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.
